I’m 58 this year, and I’ve farmed Quzhou land for 30 years, so I won’t do anything too risky. On my 19.1 mu, I’ll still keep the main part in wheat-maize double cropping, because that’s the steadiest way to get grain and cash, and I know this system well. I’ll leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton spreads the risk a bit and the work times are not exactly the same. Since I only have 3 people in the household, labor has to be arranged tightly, especially in June when wheat harvest and maize planting come together. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll irrigate at the important stages, not casually.

For wheat, the field is already in from last autumn, so this season I mainly care about topdressing, watering, and disease control. I usually do a bit more than the extension man says, because if wheat goes yellow and weak, yield drops fast. I’ll give one more nitrogen topdress around jointing, then one irrigation with it, and if the weather turns dry again I’ll water once more around heading or grain filling. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll plant summer maize right away, no delay, otherwise I lose moisture and yield. For maize I’ll use hybrid seed, put part of the fertilizer at sowing and part at the big bell stage, and usually irrigate once or twice depending on rain. Cotton I’ll keep on the smaller plot. Cotton needs more careful field watching and several pickings, but input pressure is a bit more spread out. I won’t push fertilizer too high on cotton this year because cash is not unlimited, and grain still comes first for stability.
